title: Ifosfamide and etoposide for Ewing sarcoma or osteosarcoma
context_label: Relapsed Ewing sarcoma, or treatment of osteosarcoma under the national source indication
indication_text: Relapsed Ewing sarcoma, or treatment of osteosarcoma under the national source indication
purpose: The two medicines damage tumour genetic material through different mechanisms to help control sarcoma. The intended role, chance of benefit and how this fits with surgery, radiotherapy or trials depend on the diagnosis and previous treatment.
schedule_label: Etoposide then ifosfamide on days 1–5; repeat every 21 days, up to 7 cycles
schedule_summary: Etoposide 100 mg/m² is infused over 60 minutes, followed by ifosfamide 1,800 mg/m² over 60 minutes, on each of days 1–5. Courses repeat every 21 days for up to seven cycles while benefit and tolerability justify treatment. Mesna is given before each ifosfamide infusion and at 4 and 8 hours measured from its START.
administration_text: The daily sequence includes etoposide, protective mesna, then ifosfamide, with further mesna at the prescribed times. Hydration starts before the first ifosfamide dose and continues for 24 hours after the last dose ends. Monitoring and supportive treatment make attendance longer than the drug infusion times.

agents.name: Ifosfamide
agents.mechanism: A liver-activated medicine damages genetic material
agents.explanation: The liver converts ifosfamide into active compounds that crosslink DNA, the genetic material, preventing normal cell division. Other breakdown products can damage the bladder, kidneys or brain. Mesna reduces bladder injury; it does not prevent kidney injury or brain toxicity.
agents.watch: New confusion, unusual sleepiness, hallucinations, unsteadiness, seizures, blood in urine or reduced urine needs immediate assessment.
risks: Low blood counts, serious infection or sepsis, anaemia and bleeding
Nausea, vomiting, mouth soreness, hair loss and fatigue
Brain toxicity, called encephalopathy: confusion, drowsiness, hallucinations or seizures; may be severe
Kidney tubular injury, electrolyte loss and reduced kidney function, which may persist
Bladder inflammation and bleeding despite protective mesna; report blood or pain when passing urine
Possible heart or lung injury, allergic reactions, fertility and pregnancy harm, and later cancers

agents.name: Etoposide
agents.mechanism: Prevents repair of breaks in genetic material
agents.explanation: Etoposide interferes with topoisomerase II, an enzyme that controls breaks in DNA, the genetic material. Damaged tumour cells cannot divide normally. The bone marrow and other healthy tissues are also affected.
agents.watch: Tell the nurse immediately about dizziness, flushing, rash, chest tightness, breathlessness or feeling faint during infusion.
risks: Low blood counts, serious infection or sepsis, anaemia and bleeding
Nausea, vomiting, appetite loss, mouth soreness, diarrhoea or constipation
Allergic or severe infusion reactions and low blood pressure, especially if given too quickly
Local inflammation or tissue damage around the infusion site; liver effects and rare severe skin reactions
Fertility and pregnancy harm and uncommon later blood cancers

anatomy: New confusion, unusual sleepiness, hallucinations, unsteadiness or seizures needs immediate assessment.
Report ulcers, painful swallowing or difficulty eating and drinking early.
New breathlessness, chest pain, palpitations, faintness or swelling needs urgent assessment.
Report reduced urine or inability to drink. Kidney damage and electrolyte losses may need extra tests.
Report blood or pain when passing urine immediately. Mesna reduces bladder injury but does not remove all risk.
Fever, shaking chills, sudden illness or unusual bleeding requires immediate oncology advice.
Use prescribed anti-sickness support; report persistent vomiting, severe diarrhoea or difficulty drinking.
Hair and skin changes may occur. Report line-site pain, burning, swelling or a severe rash immediately.

monitoring_schedule.note: The national regimen, product information and individual clinical plan may require different tests. Your treating team writes the actual dates and reviews results before treatment.

monitoring_test_details.label: Full blood count
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Assess infection risk, anaemia and bleeding risk.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Before starting and before each 21-day cycle; extra testing follows fever, bleeding or abnormal results. Ifosfamide product information additionally specifies counts before each administration and appropriate intervals afterwards; the team reconciles the daily course monitoring.

monitoring_test_details.label: Kidney and liver tests
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Assess drug handling and detect organ injury.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Before starting and before each cycle. Kidney filtration and tubular function also need assessment during and after ifosfamide, with timing intensified for abnormal results or symptoms.

monitoring_test_details.label: Neurological assessment
monitoring_test_details.timing: Before EVERY ifosfamide dose and urgently for new confusion, sleepiness, hallucinations, unsteadiness or seizures.

monitoring_test_details.label: Urine checks for blood
monitoring_test_details.timing: Before each ifosfamide dose and every 8 hours on treatment days; report blood or urinary pain immediately.

monitoring_test_details.label: Fluid balance and weight
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Detect low urine output, fluid retention and dehydration.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Monitor fluid balance during treatment and record weight daily. Prescribed hydration begins before ifosfamide and continues for 24 hours after the final ifosfamide infusion ends.

monitoring_test_details.label: Tumour, symptom and function review
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Assess benefit separately from treatment safety.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Before continuation at the specialist-set review points; scan timing depends on the individual Ewing sarcoma or osteosarcoma treatment plan.

monitoring_test_details.label: Sodium, potassium and phosphate
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Detect electrolyte losses including ifosfamide tubular injury.
monitoring_test_details.timing: At baseline and as regular tests with treatment-cycle reviews; repeat during treatment or recovery when results, fluid balance or symptoms require.

monitoring_test_details.label: Blood pressure and etoposide reaction monitoring
monitoring_test_details.timing: Monitor during infusion, especially the first 15 minutes. Tell staff immediately about dizziness, flushing, breathlessness or feeling faint.

support.title: Preparation and support medicines
support.text: Confirm mesna, hydration, white-cell growth-factor support and the complete five-day anti-sickness plan. Review interactions including aprepitant with ifosfamide. The source identifies this etoposide indication as unlicensed in Ireland: the patient must be informed and consented under hospital policy, with acknowledgement by the local Drugs and Therapeutics Committee or equivalent. This combination has high overall nausea/vomiting risk and requires white-cell growth-factor support for every cycle, timed by local prescription. Mesna reduces bladder injury but does not protect the kidneys or brain. Pharmacy must review anti-sickness interactions, particularly aprepitant, and specify all delayed and rescue treatment.

support.text: The team chooses appropriate intravenous access and explains its care. Report pain, burning, redness or swelling during treatment immediately. Never change pump settings or disconnect an infusion yourself.

evidence.title: Historical phase II ifosfamide/etoposide study in recurrent tumours of children and young adults
evidence.summary: A historical single-arm study showed tumour shrinkage in some previously treated patients, including small groups with Ewing sarcoma and osteosarcoma. The lack of a comparison group and very small disease-specific groups limit the estimate of benefit for today’s individual patient.
evidence.intro: A historical single-arm study showed tumour shrinkage in some previously treated patients, including small groups with Ewing sarcoma and osteosarcoma. The lack of a comparison group and very small disease-specific groups limit the estimate of benefit for today’s individual patient.
evidence.caveat: Of 124 enrolled patients, 77 were evaluable for response. Mixed tumour types, small subgroups and short follow-up limit interpretation. The trial’s longer course must not replace the current national maximum of seven cycles. Response does not establish improved survival.
evidence.interpretation: Of 124 enrolled patients, 77 were evaluable for response. Mixed tumour types, small subgroups and short follow-up limit interpretation. The trial’s longer course must not replace the current national maximum of seven cycles. Response does not establish improved survival.

questions.q: Does a delay mean treatment has failed?
questions.a: No. Blood counts, organ function and symptoms can make a delay or dose change safer. Your team decides whether and when to give the next dose.

questions.q: Who do I contact if unwell?
questions.a: Use your verified oncology daytime or out-of-hours number. If you cannot reach the team, seek urgent medical assessment. Severe symptoms require 112/999.

questions.q: Can treatment restart when a blood test improves?
questions.a: Only when the treating team confirms a new plan. A previous serious reaction, stopped medicine or required protective treatment still matters.
